title: Constitution of Lebanon adopted
why: Base text still in force, amended in 1927, 1943, 1947 and 1990.

title: Senate abolished; legislature becomes unicameral
why: Early amendment ending the bicameral structure.

title: Census records a 51% Christian majority
why: Last census; its numbers underpin confessional quotas that have outlasted the demography.

title: Unwritten National Pact sets sectarian allocation of offices
why: Maronite president, Sunni PM, Shia speaker; 6:5 parliament ratio based on 1932 census.

title: Constitution amended on the flag's cedar colour
why: Date corrected from a broader Nov 1943 claim, which no opened source confirms.

title: Shia Muslims get the speakership of parliament
why: Wikipedia dates the allocation to 1947; it became part of the National Pact practice.

title: Banking secrecy law promulgated
why: Bound bankers against all authorities; Law 200/2020 cites it as dated 3 Sep 1956.

title: Kaza-based electoral law adopted
why: District system behind the 1964-72 elections; the 2008 Doha deal reverted to it.

title: Code of Money and Credit creates Banque du Liban
why: Decree 13513 of 1 Aug 1963, the foundation of the central bank.

title: Banque du Liban starts operating
why: Only 2.5 years old when Intra failed in 1966 and it declined to lend.

title: Intra Bank collapses
why: Held 15% of deposits; BDL refused liquidity. Triggered the post-Intra banking regime.

title: Law 2/67 adds special provisions for insolvent banks
why: Reported by a search summary of Lexology; page not opened.

title: Law 28/67 creates National Deposit Guarantee Institution
why: Protects small depositors up to a ceiling; reported by a search summary, not opened.

title: Cairo Agreement regulates PLO presence in Lebanon
why: Brokered by Nasser; text never officially published, a leaked version ran in An-Nahar on 20 Apr 1970.

title: Parliament abrogates the Cairo Agreement
why: Approved 21 May and signed in June 1987 by Gemayel and Hoss.

title: Taif Agreement signed
why: National Reconciliation Accord ending the civil war; ratified by parliament on 5 Nov 1989.

title: Parliament ratifies Taif; Moawad elected president
why: Parliament elected Rene Moawad president the same day.

title: Taif constitutional amendments enacted
why: 1:1 parity and power shifted from the president to the cabinet.

title: Taif deadline for militia disbandment
why: Deadline to surrender territory and heavy weapons, the legal root of the later arms dispute.

title: General Amnesty Law 84/91
why: Covers crimes before 28 Mar 1991; no civil-war prosecutions followed. Sources could not be opened.

title: Constitutional Council set up
why: Creation year not confirmed in this research; law number left blank.

title: Riad Salameh becomes BDL governor
why: Served 30 years to 31 July 2023; his tenure ended in charges and sanctions.

title: Naturalisation Decree 5247 grants citizenship to about 150,000
why: Date corrected from 22 June (other sources); Globalcit gives 20 June. Contested on sectarian-balance grounds.

title: State Consultative Council rules many 1994 grants unlawful
why: Found citizenship granted to people who failed legal requirements.

title: UN Security Council Resolution 1757 creates the STL
why: Chapter VII route after parliament stalled on the Hariri tribunal.

title: Doha Agreement signed; Suleiman elected 25 May
why: Ended an 18-month crisis; adopted the kaza as constituency per the 1960 law.

title: Special Tribunal for Lebanon opens
why: Took over from the UN investigation commission.

title: Law 132 on offshore petroleum resources
why: Framework for licensing; gazetted 2 Sep 2010, Official Gazette 41.

title: Decrees 6690 and 6691 revoke 176 irregular naturalisations
why: Signed by President Suleiman; based on falsified documents.

title: Parliament extends own term by 17 months to 20 Nov 2014
why: First self-extension; the last election before it was June 2009.

title: Constitutional Council calls periodic elections an absolute principle
why: Yet the extension stood; HRW says the ruling made a later extension unlawful.

title: Law 293 on protection from family violence
why: Dated 7 May 2014; amended by Law 204/2020.

title: Parliament extends to 20 June 2017
why: Second extension; Aoun's bloc petitioned the Constitutional Council eight days later.

title: Law 44 on anti-money laundering and terrorist financing
why: Dated 24 Nov 2015, Official Gazette 48; Law 42 covers cross-border cash and Law 53 the TF convention.

title: Law 62 creates the National Human Rights Institution
why: Includes the torture prevention committee; amended by Law 273/2022.

title: Law 28 on the right to access information
why: Passed 18 Jan 2017, gazetted 16 Feb 2017 (date corrected from 2017-02).

title: Parliament passes electoral Law 44/2017
why: Session of 16 June 2017; proportional system, used in 2018 and 2022. (Law 44/2017 is dated 17 June 2017 in citing laws; 16 June is the Parliament vote)

title: Parliament passes Law 81 on e-transactions and personal data
why: Session 24 Sep 2018; search sources report promulgation on 10 Oct 2018. No independent regulator.

title: Law 83 protects corruption whistleblowers
why: Dated 10 Oct 2018; Law 182/2020 later added a paragraph to its Article 9.

title: Law 115/2019 approves the Paris Agreement
why: Number and date reported by search, inferred from neighbouring laws; not seen in text.

title: Banks impose informal capital controls; no law authorises them
why: Basis of years of depositor lawsuits; not confirmed on an opened page.

title: Law 175 creates the National Anti-Corruption Commission
why: Dated 8 May 2020, gazetted 14 May 2020; first statutory definition of corruption.

title: Law 182 amends the whistleblower law
why: Adds a paragraph to Article 9 of Law 83/2018.

title: STL convicts Salim Ayyash in absentia
why: Postponed from 7 Aug by the port blast; three co-accused acquitted at first instance.

title: Law 189 on financial disclosure and illicit enrichment
why: Dated 16 Oct 2020, gazetted 22 Oct (date corrected from 2020-09).

title: Law 200 suspends banking secrecy for one year
why: Opened records for the forensic audit of the central bank; extended by Law 279/2022.

title: Law 204 amends the domestic violence law
why: Amends Law 293/2014; gazetted 7 Jan 2021.

title: Law 205 criminalises sexual harassment
why: Dated 30 Dec 2020, gazetted 7 Jan 2021 (date corrected from 2020-12).

title: Law 212 extends the asset-declaration deadline
why: Extends filing under Law 189/2020, showing slow implementation.

title: Law 214 on recovery of assets from corruption crimes
why: Dated 8 Apr 2021, gazetted 15 Apr 2021.

title: Public Procurement Law 244 enacted
why: Dated 19 July 2021; in force 29 July 2022 (date corrected from 2021-06-30).

title: Judge Ghada Aoun subpoenas Salameh; illicit enrichment charge
why: Early domestic case against the BDL governor; he faced charges in March 2022.

title: STL appeals chamber convicts Merhi and Oneissi
why: Reversed acquittals; search-reported, date not confirmed.

title: Law 279 extends Law 200/2020 until the forensic audit ends
why: Keeps banking secrecy suspended for the audit; dated 7 Mar 2022.

title: Law 290 suspends deadlines on distressed loans
why: Debtor relief during the crisis; Official Gazette 14 Apr 2022.

title: Procurement law takes effect
why: Entry into force confirmed by the 2023 amending law.

title: Law 306 amends banking secrecy and the Code of Money and Credit
why: Confirmed as dated 28 Oct 2022 by the 2025 law that amends it.

title: Parliament amends eight articles of the procurement law
why: Amends articles 7, 11, 19, 46, 60, 76, 100 and 101; session of 18 Apr 2023; law number illegible.

title: Salameh's BDL term ends; forensic audit finds $111M commissions
why: Audit documented a reported $76B loss masked by financial engineering.

title: US, UK and Canada sanction Salameh
why: Followed years of domestic and European investigations.

title: Capital-controls session fails: 53 of 128 MPs attend
why: FPM and LF boycotted; the bill never returned to plenary.

title: STL closure announced by the UN
why: Date corrected from 2024-01-01; three convicted men remain at large.

title: Law suspends legal, judicial and contractual deadlines
why: Covers 8 Oct 2023 onwards for war-affected parties.

title: Port-blast probe resumes after Salam is named prime minister
why: Obstacles fell after prosecutor changes; TIMEP says Hajjar lifted bans.

title: Karim Souaid takes over as BDL governor
why: First governor after the Mansouri interim, amid the IMF-driven reform push.

title: Parliament lifts banking secrecy in effect
why: Amends article 7 of the 1956 law and article 150 of the Code of Money and Credit, ten-year look-back.

title: Law amends Code of Money and Credit articles 4, 5 and 6
why: Reworks BDL governance; passed the same day as the secrecy amendment.

title: Bitar expected to indict on 4 August 2025; deadline passes
why: Wikipedia reported the plan; no indictment followed that year.

title: Parliament passes the bank resolution bill
why: IMF prerequisite since 2020; shareholders bear losses first; TIMEP criticises banking-lobby control.

title: Parliament adopts the judicial independence law
why: More judicial self-governance; HRW says the prosecutor can still halt proceedings.

title: Speaker signs judicial law; it takes effect January 2026
why: Sent to the PM and President for promulgation.

title: Bank resolution promulgated as Law 23/2025
why: Official Gazette 36 of 21 Aug 2025 (date corrected from 31 July, the vote date).

title: Bulgaria arrests Rhosus shipowner on Interpol request
why: Key port-blast development; Igor Grechushkin was detained.

title: Aoun asks parliament to reconsider the judicial law
why: Aoun cited procedural, substantive and material errors; parliament adopted an amended law on 18 Dec 2025.

title: Cabinet approves draft law creating MITAI
why: Cabinet session of 9 Sep 2025 approved the draft law (Decree 1286); Enmaeya reported it on 15 Sep. First new ministry since 1993.

title: Cabinet approves the financial gap law 13 to 9
why: Dated Friday 26 Dec 2025 (date corrected from 27 Dec); $100k deposits repaid, rest via bonds.

title: Court finds ex-ministers Khalil and Zaiter guilty of obstruction
why: Civil finding in the port-blast obstruction saga.

title: Parliament passes the 2026 budget law
why: Passed at the 27 Jan 2026 session.

title: Decree 2438 schedules elections for 1-10 May 2026
why: Diaspora on 1 and 3 May, domestic vote on 10 May. (law number unconfirmed)

title: Lawmakers table a bill to extend the term by two years
why: Grounds: security, logistics and electoral-framework issues, per Lexis. (vote to extend 9 March 2026 confirmed; tabling on 3 March not confirmed)

title: Parliament extends its term two years, 76 to 41
why: Runs to 31 May 2028; Khalaf calls it unconstitutional; no article cited for force majeure.

title: Judge Bitar concludes the port-blast investigation
why: 70 people charged; file sent to Prosecutor Hajjar.

title: Cabinet approves amendments to Law 23/2025
why: Date corrected from 1 May; two articles changed after IMF consultation.

title: Parliament sends the MITAI bill to joint committees
why: MTV reported the referral to joint committees on 15 Jul 2026 (exact session day not stated); SMEX criticised the bill on 31 Jul 2026.

title: Parliament passes the amended bank restructuring law
why: Decree 6503 amending Law 36/1930; article 3 fell, article 11 in government text.

title: Prosecutor Saab submits 270-page opinion to Judge Bitar
why: Final indictment pending; a lawyer expects it before year end. Search-reported. (corrected from 2026-09-21; Arab News says Tuesday, dated 16 Sep, but 16 Sep 2026 is a Wednesday, so Tuesday 15 Sep inferred; Yeni Safak of 21 Sep says 'last week')

title: Financial gap law still unpassed as IMF staff deal awaited
why: Full programme hinges on it; fetch of the source timed out.
